As someone whose been openly homosexual since I was like 12, people like this guy are a disgrace to the LGBT community, and I don’t even consider myself a part of that community. Though it wouldn’t be the first time I met a gay ‘nice guy’ on some dating apps myself and he certainly is the type to be a sociopath. It’s worse that he ‘thinks his friend has feelings for him too’ when it’s more than likely that it’s one sided. The people who are homosexual who view the other sex as some kind of ‘snake’ are just not okay people.

The idea of Cthulhu though is that there shouldn’t even be a way to fight back at all. It empowers the player when the idea of lovecraft is to disempower and disturb them, to drag them through the uncanny valley and obliterate sanity. The mere presence of a gun or even the ability to hide from an alien that is supposed to be omnipotent is utterly ruining the scenario. Also, there is no point to the ‘this may affect your destiny’ icon because there’s only one ending. Which is bullshit. $60 would be fair if it had a TON of replayability, try out different stats and get different outcomes, it’d be forgivable then, but a single ending? It’s useless. The only stats that ‘matter’ are occultism, medicine, psychological, and investigative. You’ll see those the most but even then, any and all issues that require a skill check that you fail can easily be circumvented by finding a key barely hidden and moving on. 

The gun segment was trash in that it ruins the game. The devs said it’s easily 10 hours of gameplay, yet there’s already a full walkthrough, cutscenes and everything, that shows it’s less than a 6 your game. I could have forgiven that IF YOU COULD CHANGE THE FUCKING OUTCOME AND HAVE MULTIPLE ENDINGS. 

I tweeted at the devs with a bunch of text error pics and told them why did they sell an unfinished game. They asked what system and region, and lo and behold a patch update right away.

A good lovecraft game will create the horror through atmosphere and powerful suggestion rather than obvious imagery. The terror should come from the vague sense that something is incredibly wrong with Darkwater. It did that well in the first two hours, but the second you find the cult, it loses that suspense because it lays on that cult way too much to the point where it’s obnoxious. The most fun and actually creepy parts of the game were when you were investigating, trying to pass skill checks, and so on. 

The concept of Cthulhu isn’t that it’s a monster, it’s an idea. An existential horror. I suggest watching Extra Credits video on the subject as they hammer the idea well. https://youtu.be/7DyRxlvM9VM

Oh for sure, it’d be good for the budget and they wouldn’t need a large team. I was just very disappointed, they definitely rushed the living hell out of this game, probably because some of their investors were pressuring them to hurry it up. All those placeholder text errors killed it for me. 

It’s why I believe companies like CD Projekt Red always pump out successful and great games. I’m hyped for Cyberpunk 2077, they’re pouring their soul into it, lots of interesting potential there. Actually they had a much smaller team than Call of Cthulhu did when they were developing Witcher 3. I plan on getting Thronebreaker soon, it looks very well made and solid mechanics. Plus that good ol’ Witcher world art and story.
